traits: Cap 4 to 20 cm, wine-red to purple with a carmine edge and a blackish-purple centre, sometimes greenish
Gills nearly free, cream, yellowing with age, with purplish edges
Stem 4 to 12 cm, white, sometimes tinged red, browning when bruised
Smell of boiled crab or shrimp, stronger with age; mild taste
Mostly under conifers, spruce, pine or fir · summer to autumn
safetyNote: Edible: the DGfM and the VAPKO list it. Wikipedia (en) counts it among the best edibles of its genus, young caps being good for stuffing; Wikipedia (fr) places it among the edibles but finds its crayfish or herring taste unappealing. The shellfish smell stays when cooked (Wikipedia, en). The sickener has a white stem and white gills (Wikipedia, en): see the group.

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
